Igon was once a poor scavenger of battlefields, but found honour in the ancient art of Dragon Communion, whereby hunters of dragons could consume their hearts to gain their strength.
Igon soon became a fearless drake warrior and set his eyes on the greatest prey of all: Bayle the Dread, progenitor of the drakes, and the very reason that Dragon Communion had been created. Driven by bottomless hunger and fiery ambition, Igon journeyed to Bayle's roost at the top of the Jagged Peak to challenge the dragon. However, Igon found himself outmatched. Despite this, Igon willed himself to climb back towards the Jagged Peak. Here he encountered a Tarnished champion also hunting for Bayle. Igon begged the Tarnished to summon his soul when facing Bayle so that he might have his revenge. Together, the two drake warriors succeed in slaying Bayle, allowing Igon to die in peace.

Dane is a member of the Dryleaf Sect, an order of spiritual seekers who chose to serve a new god after seeing the decline of the Erdtree in the fallen leaves. Dane fights using an unarmed technique which focuses on kicks.
Dane is a compatriot of Needle Knight Leda, and has been in the service of Miquella even longer than she has. He seldom speaks, and even Leda has never heard his voice. The The Tarnished may challenge him to a duel in Scadu Altus, after which he will grant them access to Dryleaf Arts. He can optionally be summoned to fight against Romina, Saint of the Bud at the Church of the Bud.
Dane discovers the sealing tree in the Ancient Ruins of Rauh and deduces that it must be burnt using the flame of Messmer the Impaler. After it has been burnt, Dane joins Leda in Enir-Ilim, where they face off against the Tarnished. Upon his defeat he finally breaks his silence, offering a plea for Miquella to rise to godhood.

author_evidence.quote:
Formerly the feared commander of the Pureblood Knights in service of Lord Mohg, Ansbach is one of the compatriots of Needle Knight Leda who followed Miquella into the Realm of Shadow. Ansbach has dedicated himself to investigating Miquella's purpose by following the trail of crosses he left behind.
As with the rest who followed Miquella into the Shadow Realm, Ansbach was under the influence of a charm, which breaks when the Empyrean abandons his Miquella's Great Rune. With his mind freed of the charm, Ansbach recalls that he once challenged Miquella in an attempt to free Mohg of his enchantment, which resulted in him falling under the enchantment himself.
With his faculties restored, Ansbach makes his way to the Specimen Storehouse within the Shadow Keep. There, he learns that Mohg's body has been taken to Miquella, and with the assistance of the Tarnished discovers that Miquella intends to use Mohg's corpse as a vessel for his king consort.
Ansbach becomes one of Leda's possible targets, resulting in a duel which the Tarnished may intervene in on either side. Should Ansbach survive Leda's attack, he will aid the Tarnished against Leda, Dryleaf Dane, and their allies in Enir-Ilim. Ansbach will then be available to assist the Tarnished in their battle against Promised Consort Radahn, before which he admits that he knows the Tarnished was responsible for killing Mohg, but bears no grudge against them, viewing Mohg's death as an honorable one. After defeating Miquella and his consort, Ansbach dies in front of the Gate of Divinity.

Gurranq is a hulking, bestial clergyman who resides in the Bestial Sanctum in north-eastern Caelid. Long ago, his terrifying ferocity earned him the name "Death of the Demigods. Presently, he seeks Deathroot, a product of the Rune of Death which spread through the Lands Between following the murder of Godwyn the Golden on the Night of Black Knives. Gurranq consumes Deathroot, although it does not appear to sate him.
Gurranq was assisted in his eradication of the Deathroot by D, Hunter of the Dead, a hunter of Those Who Live in Death. However, D passes this duty onto a Tarnished after noticing their prowess for weeding Deathroot. The Tarnished brings the Deathroot they find throughout the world to Gurranq, and is given access to bestial incantations in exchange. Once they have fed Gurranq all the Deathroot they can find, Gurranq leaves the sanctum. Although still not sated, he realises that he can do no more, and that his appetite will be his sole companion.
When the Tarnished travels to Crumbling Farum Azula to claim the Rune of Death, they encounter Gurranq once more. If the Tarnished had given Gurraq all the Deathroots, he is saddened by his friend's betrayal, but nonetheless attacks the Tarnished to protect the Rune of Death from them. Gurraq is overwhelmed, forcing him to use the Rune of Death to empower himself and reveal his true form as Maliketh, the Black Blade, shadowbound beast of Queen Marika the Eternal. The Tarnished defeats Maliketh, and unleashes the Rune of Death.

Next, Alexander travels to Mt. Gelmir, hoping to temper his body in the sea of fire such that it would never crack again. Finding the lava to be lukewarm and insufficient to strengthen his vessel, he sets his sights upon the Mountaintops of the Giants, seeking out the flame of ruin.

Formerly one of the most distinguished knights of Starscourge Radahn, who invited her into his ranks after witnessing her valour as a gladiator, Freyja is one of the compatriots of Needle Knight Leda who followed Miquella into the Realm of Shadow.
In the past, Freyja was stricken by Scarlet Rot in the Swamp of Aeonia. Left behind and resigned to death, she was approached by Miquella, who put his lips to her wound and drained the poison from it. Freyja was subsequently charmed by Miquella, and later entered the Realm of Shadow with Leda and her compatriots.
After Miquella's charm is broken, Freyja chooses to strike out on her own, although she remains loyal to Miquella. She recalls Miquella mentioning a vow he once made with her former lord Radahn, and resolves to learn the nature of the vow. To this end, she travels to the Shadow Keep, where she has difficulty reading the letters etched into the stone tablets. With assistance from the The Tarnished and Sir Ansbach, Freyja learns that Miquella wishes to revive the soul of General Radahn. Freyja welcomes this, believing that endless war would suit her former master better than an honourable death.
Later, Freyja joins Leda and Dryleaf Dane in Enir-Ilim, in their fight against the Tarnished. Upon her defeat, she praises the Tarnished for providing her with a glorious battle.

Map of Ainsel River
One of the two great rivers that flow beneath the Lands Between. Ainsel is said to be the grave of civilisations that flourished before the Erdtree. The eastern side of Ainsel is dominated by the Uhl Palace Ruins, characterised by their mausoleums and statues, and inhabited by the Claymen who served as priests of the ancient dynasty.
Nokstella, one of the Eternal Cities, can be found in the western portion of the subterranean space, inhabited by the Nox who were banished underground by the Greater Will long ago. Deeper still is the Lake of Rot, a putrid underground swamp littered with ancient ruins, where the essence of an Outer God was sealed. At the deepest point is the lair of Astel, a malformed star who once assailed an Eternal City and took away its sky. Beyond Astel is a lift which leads to the Moonlight Altar, provided the Dark Moon Ring has been found.
Ainsel can be accessed via the Ainsel River Well in eastern Liurnia of the Lakes. The Ainsel River Main, which encompasses Nokstella, can be accessed via a sending gate in Renna's Rise, after Ranni the Witch gets her hands on the Fingerslayer Blade.

author_evidence.quote:
Brother Corhyn is a cleric of the Golden Order, who was granted the guidance of Grace due to his iron will and unwavering faith in the face of his exile. At some point, Corhyn made his way to Roundtable Hold, where he teaches the incantations of the Two Fingers to Tarnished of the Roundtable, hoping that one of them might one day claim the title of Elden Lord, so that Corhyn might council them. When a Tarnished champion makes their way to the Roundtable, Corhyn introduces himself to them, and offers his tutelage. Corhyn will even teach the champion heretical incantations, from outside the line of the Erdtree, though he does so reluctantly.
After the Tarnished champion opens the way to the Altus Plateau, Corhyn announces that he is departing the Roundtable to search for the legendary Goldmask, an eminent scholar of the Golden Order. While searching for Goldmask, Corhyn continues his own investigations into the nature of the Golden Order, and while he makes some advancements, he also becomes aware of how little he truly knows. With guidance from the Tarnished champion, Corhyn is united with Goldmask.
Corhyn takes it upon himself to become Goldmask's disciple and to chronicle his wisdom, deciphering the meaning behind every minute movement made by the mute Goldmask. The process goes well, until Goldmask's movements suddenly cease, as he is confounded by the nature of Radagon. The Tarnished champion may solve the riddle, revealing to Goldmask that Radagon and Queen Marika the Eternal are in fact one and the same, allowing Corhyn to continue his work.

author_evidence.quote:
A snow-swept, misty area to the west of the Mountaintops of the Giants. The Consecrated Snowfield is final trial for those who seek Miquella's Haligtree, and can only be accessed by uniting the two halves of the Haligtree Secret Medallion, found in the Village of the Albinaurics and Castle Sol, and bringing them to the Grand Lift of Rold.
Visibility is limited in many parts of the snowfield. Small, golden lights illuminate the path from the upper section to the broad, snowy plane below, through which a frozen river runs. In the south-west are the Yelough Anix Ruins, consumed by the Flame of Frenzy. Far to the north lies the Apostate Derelict, where the gentle yet towering sister of Latenna the Albinauric resides. South-east of there is Ordina, Liturgical Town, which hides the entrance to the Haligtree. There is also a waygate, tucked away on the western cliffs, which leads to Mohgwyn Palace.

A small town in the north of the Consecrated Snowfield. Ordina is the final stop on the path to Miquella's Haligtree, although to gain entry, one must dispel a magical barrier. An Evergaol on the north side of town will allow the player to enter a version of the town inhabited by many Albinauric Archers, as well as two invisible Black Knife Assassins. There are four candles held by statues in the town, which must be lit in order to open the way to the Haligtree. The candles will remain lit even if the player dies after lighting them.
In the regular version of the town, the spirits of the Albinauric Archers, their wolves, and the assassins, can be seen wandering through the streets, although they cannot be fought or interacted with.
